title: Macleods, Amneal Recall Olanzapine, Exenatide Products in US Over Quality Issues
summary: New Delhi: Macleods Pharmaceuticals Ltd has initiated a voluntary recall of 15,744 bottles of Olanzapine Tablets, USP 2.5 mg in the United States after the product failed impurities and degradation...

contentHtml:
New Delhi: Macleods Pharmaceuticals Ltd has initiated a voluntary recall of 15,744 bottles of Olanzapine Tablets, USP 2.5 mg in the United States after the product failed impurities and degradation specifications.

The recall involves 30-count bottles of the prescription medicine manufactured by Macleods Pharmaceuticals Ltd at its facility in Baddi, Himachal Pradesh, India.

The recalled product is Olanzapine Tablets, USP 2.5 mg, supplied in a 30-count bottle and marked Rx Only. The product was manufactured for Macleods Pharma USA, Inc., Princeton, New Jersey 08540, and manufactured by Macleods Pharmaceuticals Ltd, Baddi, Himachal Pradesh, India. The product carries NDC 33342-067-07.

According to the recall information, the product was recalled because it failed impurities/degradation specifications. The affected product is identified under Lot No. BOB12318A, with an expiry date of July 31, 2027. The recall involves 15,744 30-count bottles and is listed under Recall Number D-0154-2025.

The US recall is classified as a Class II recall. The action was initiated voluntarily by the firm, with the initial notification to consignees or the public issued through a letter. The distribution pattern for the affected Olanzapine product was nationwide in the United States.

The recall record identifies the recalling firm as Macleods Pharmaceuticals Ltd, 304 Atlanta Arcade, Church Road, Mumbai, India. The recall was initiated on November 25, 2024, while the Center Classification Date was December 19, 2024. The recall remains ongoing, and no termination date has been provided.

Olanzapine is a second-generation antipsychotic medication used in the treatment of mental health conditions including schizophrenia and bipolar disorders. The recalled product therefore concerns a prescription medicine distributed across the US market.

The recall information lists Event ID 95838 and states that a press release was not issued for the recall. The record also identifies the product type as Drugs. The update history associated with the recall provides the above product, manufacturing, distribution, classification and event information.

Separately, Amneal Pharmaceuticals of New York, LLC has initiated a voluntary recall of 5,694 Exenatide Injection prefilled pens in the US. According to the FDA enforcement record contained in the supplied spreadsheet, the recalled product is Exenatide Injection, USP, 250 mcg/mL, 1.2 mL per prefilled pen, intended for subcutaneous use and single-patient use.

The Amneal product was manufactured by Amneal Pharmaceuticals Pvt. Ltd., Ahmedabad 382213, India, and distributed by Amneal Pharmaceuticals LLC, Bridgewater, New Jersey 08807. The product carries NDC 70121-1685-1. The affected lot is AP250095A, with an expiry date of February 28, 2027.

The reason for the Amneal recall is a defective delivery system, with the possibility that there may be no medication in the prefilled pen. The FDA classified the action as a Class II recall. The recall number is D-0868-2026, and the recall was initiated on August 28, 2026. The Center Classification Date was September 22, 2026, while the report date was September 30, 2026.

The Amneal recall is also listed as voluntary and firm initiated, with initial notification through a letter and distribution across the US nationwide market. The recalling firm is Amneal Pharmaceuticals of New York, LLC, located at 50 Horseblock Rd, Brookhaven, New York 11719-9509. The recall status is listed as ongoing, with no termination date reported.

Exenatide is a once-weekly medicine that mimics the GLP-1 hormone and is used along with diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus. The Macleods and Amneal actions therefore involve two different prescription medicines and separate product-quality issues reported in the US drug market.
